turns.question: Is it a living organism (or a part of one)?

evidence.excerpt: An eyebrow is an area of short terminal hairs above each eye that follows the shape of the lower margin of the brow ridges of some mammals. In humans, eyebrows serve two main functions: first, prevention of sweat, water, and other debris from falling down into the eye socket, and second, communication through facial expression.

Eyebrow hairs ... are the arch of terminal hair located on the brow—the soft tissue overlying the bony supraorbital ridge, at the junction of the frontalis and orbicularis oculi muscles. They are among the first visible terminal hairs to develop during embryogenesis and are present from birth onward. The page classifies them under human anatomy, integument, skin appendages, and hairs.
